transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve just been really jumpy lately. At work, if a door slams or someone rushes by with a suitcase in the lobby, I kind of… jump like it’s happening again. It takes a bit for my heart to settle down after.
Can you tell me what you mean by 'happening again'?
I mean… I get this image in my head, out of nowhere. That guest leaning over the counter, knocking the equipment toward me. Sometimes it happens when I’m just trying to answer a normal call.
Did the incident with the guest leaning over the counter and knocking equipment toward you actually happen to you?
Yeah… it happened. I mean, that part was real. I don’t really like talking about it, but yes.
Do these images in your head happen even when you're trying not to think about them?
Yeah. I try not to think about it, but it still just… pops in. Like I’m on a regular call and suddenly I see him leaning over the counter again, knocking things toward me.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because of these images or the incident?
Yeah… I guess I have. I’ve been using the back hallway when I can. Walking past that spot in the lobby where it happened just… makes my chest tighten, and I want to get away from it.
Do you have trouble sleeping at night?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I haven’t noticed anything major with sleep.
Do you find yourself being easily startled by things that wouldn't normally startle you, like a loud noise or an unexpected touch?
Yeah… more than I’d like. If a door slams, or someone rolls a suitcase fast across the lobby, I just jump. It feels like it’s happening again for a second, and it takes me a minute to calm down.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the incident with the guest, like it's actually happening all over again, not just seeing it in your head?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get the image in my head sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like I’m actually back there or anything.
How long have you been experiencing these jumpy feelings and images in your head?
About two weeks, I think… since that guest threatened me at the front desk. It’s kind of been there since then.
Have you avoided any social activities or relationships because of what happened?
Not really… I don’t think so. I’ve kind of kept to myself a bit, but I wouldn’t say I’m avoiding people or anything like that.
Have you stopped doing anything you used to enjoy because it reminds you of the incident or makes you feel anxious?
Yeah… a little. I’ve been using the back hallway when I can. Walking past that spot in the lobby just… makes my chest tighten, and I want to get away from it.
Have you avoided talking about the incident with friends or family?

Yeah… I mean, I haven’t really talked much about it. Mostly I just try not to deal with it—like at work, I take the back hallway when I can so I don’t have to pass that spot in the lobby. It just makes my chest tighten.
Have you avoided any other places or situations besides the lobby where the incident happened?
Not really other places… mostly just that lobby area. I take the back hallway when I can, because passing that spot makes my chest tighten and I just want to get away from it.
Have you significantly changed your daily routine to avoid reminders of the incident?

Yeah… I guess mostly at work. I’ve been taking the back hallway whenever I can, just so I don’t have to walk past that spot in the lobby. It makes my chest tighten, and I just want to get away from it.
Have you found it increasingly difficult to go to work because of what happened at the front desk?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still going in. It’s just been harder. I’m slower at the reservation desk, and my manager had to cut a couple of my shifts short. I keep finding reasons not to cross the lobby when guests need help.
Have you avoided doing anything important or significant because it reminds you of the incident?

I guess… mainly at work. I’ve been avoiding walking past that spot in the lobby, taking the back hallway when I can. It’s not huge, but when I get near it my chest tightens and I just want to get away.
Have you avoided other work-related tasks or responsibilities besides walking past the spot in the lobby?

Yeah… some. I’m still showing up, but I’m slower at the reservation desk than usual. And when guests need help across the lobby, I catch myself making excuses or asking someone else. My manager’s had to shorten a couple of my shifts because of it.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I… don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed losing interest, exactly. I guess I’m just kind of doing what I have to do.
